verdict.rationale: Plausible's docs explicitly describe a self-serve funnel analysis feature (define a sequence of steps, measure drop-off, choose sequential or strict order) plus 'User journeys' to explore visitor paths, which directly maps to the founder's story of finding where activation drops off without an analyst [plausible-docs-5, plausible-docs-41, plausible-docs-42, plausible-docs-55]. However, community hands-on feedback concretely contradicts the completeness of this capability: one HN comment says Plausible 'lacks much of the information from Matomo (like after viewing /foo, visitors tend to view...)' when comparing journey/flow analysis [plausible-comm-6], and another states the founders 'refuse to adopt tracking of user flows through a website, allegedly for privacy reasons' [plausible-comm-5], suggesting the flow/journey tooling is thinner or newer than the marketing docs imply. Missing for 10: independent verification that funnel/drop-off analysis works robustly in practice, resolution of the conflicting community reports about journey-tracking depth, and evidence of founders actually using it unaided to diagnose activation drop-off.
